description.purpose: The files of one knowledge space, each a logical file hive under one address: `fh-<12 hex>` for the file, `@<hex>` for a version of it. Content lives as content-addressed blocks and immutable versions in the space's one store; every file has one main line that moves only by compare-and-swap on the version a writer read; workspaces are copy-on-write views committed in two phases. No answer names where a file lives -- moving its rows into another space's store changes no address (ADR 0047). Since 1.1.0 ([#905](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/905), [#906](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/906), [#907](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/907), [#908](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/908)) the child hive `./projection` lays a workspace out on a disk, runs a permitted program in it and carries it into git and back, `in_ingest` stores a document a channel sent, and `in_schemas`/`in_tool` put the file tools on a model's menu; lanes joined, so it is the second digit. Since 1.1.1 ([#929](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/929)) the finished document turn leaves `./ingest` for the space without restoring its TTL; the door of the generation it enters restores it. A repair, so it is the third digit. Since 1.2.0 ([#944](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/944)) the head of every file is cut into nodes with semantic anchors and extracted links, answered on the ops `outline`, `links` and `near` and on the tools `file_outline` and `file_links`, and every head that moves leaves the space as `source_changed`; a caller can ask for what it could not before, so it is the second digit.
description.use_when: Wherever text or documents have to be kept, read by line and changed by many writers without losing a change: send a request on `in_read`, `in_write` or `in_ws` of the hive path with `hop.op` and `hop.op_id`, draw `answer` back to the caller.
description.not_in_scope: No disk, `exec` or git in the hive itself -- the child hive `./projection` carries all three; no tool for `raw` or `ws_tree`; no anchors inside a file (`#...` is refused with `anchor_unsupported`); no rights -- who reaches the hive path may read and write.
examples: PORTS - every endpoint is the HIVE path (`params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed). Entry on `hop.route`: in_read, in_write, in_ws, in_model, in_schemas, in_tool. Exit: answer, model_refused, derived, tool_schemas, tool_result.

REQUEST - body `{op, file, args}`, hop `op`, `op_id` (required, mirrored), `ws` (optional workspace name), `mode` (search only), `caller` (internal callers only). Worked: {"op": "read", "file": "/notes/plan.md", "args": {"from": 1, "to": 40}} on `in_read` answers `{ok, op, op_id, file, version, lines, from, to, text}` with every line as `<n>:<h4>|<text>`.
ADDRESS - `fh-<12 hex>` or a path `/a/b.md`, optionally `@<hex prefix>`, `@ws:<name>` or `@snap:<name>`; every answer names the file by its id and the version by its first 12 hex digits.
